name: RRB Group D
fullName: Railway Recruitment Boards – Level 1 Posts (Group D) Recruitment
conductingBody: Railway Recruitment Boards / RRCs (Ministry of Railways)
approxCandidates: ≈1 crore+ applicants in recent cycles (CEN 08/2024 drew over 1 crore applications; CEN 09/2025 figure approx.)
eligibility: 10th pass or ITI / National Apprenticeship Certificate; 18–33 yrs (relaxation as per rules)

notification.summary: Current cycle is CEN 09/2025 for about 22,195 Level-1 posts (Track Maintainer, Pointsman, Assistant, Helper etc.). The CBT was held in August 2026 (3–21 Aug, with a revised schedule reportedly extending to 25 Aug), and the provisional answer key with response sheets was released on 7 Sep 2026 with objections till 15 Sep 2026. The CBT result/PET shortlist was awaited as of the check date. The previous cycle (CEN 08/2024, ~32,438 posts) held its CBT from Nov 2025 to Feb 2026.

pattern.notes: Single CBT, no sectional timing; 1/3 negative marking. Marks normalised across shifts. Minimum qualifying: UR/EWS 40%, OBC/SC 30%, ST 25%. Followed by PET (qualifying), Document Verification and Medical. Science is of Class 10 (CBSE) standard.

trendAnalysis.summary: Group D papers from the 2022 cycle, CEN 08/2024 (Nov 2025–Feb 2026) and CEN 09/2025 (Aug 2026) have been easy-to-moderate. The 25-30-25-20 split (Maths-Reasoning-Science-GA) has been unchanged. Mathematics is direct and formula-based (simplification, percentage, ratio, SI/CI, mensuration, basic trigonometry). Reasoning is the most scoring section: series, coding, analogies, blood relations, syllogism and short puzzles. General Science follows NCERT Class 9–10 with physics numericals (motion, electricity, optics) and biology facts. GA leans on current affairs (sports, schemes, awards) plus static history, polity and geography. Good attempts are typically 75–85.

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from the three most recent Group D CBT cycles: RRC 01/2019 (CBT Aug–Oct 2022), CEN 08/2024 (CBT Nov 2025–Feb 2026) and CEN 09/2025 (CBT Aug 2026). RRB bars candidates from sharing live questions, so web searches (Oct 2026) returned only shift-wise difficulty/good-attempt analyses (PracticeMock, Careers360, Adda247) with topic counts; question TYPES were therefore described from those topic lists plus the writer's own knowledge of the officially released 2022 question papers/response sheets and memory-based analyses. WebFetch of the papers themselves was not possible. Patterns are paraphrased; no real question is reproduced.

archetypes.pattern: Divisibility test – which of four large numbers is divisible by 8/9/11, or find the missing digit that makes a number divisible
Remainder and unit-digit of large powers or products (cyclicity of 2, 3, 7, 8)
Sum of first n natural/odd/even numbers, count of primes or factors in a range
Simplify an expression with "of", brackets and mixed operations; distractors from left-to-right evaluation that ignores "of"
Square roots/cube roots of perfect squares and decimals combined with basic operations
Compare/order fractions or add mixed fractions and decimals; convert recurring decimals to fractions
HCF/LCM of given numbers or fractions, and HCF × LCM = product of two numbers
Least/greatest number leaving the same remainder, bells tolling together – LCM/HCF word problems
Divide an amount in a given (or fractional) ratio; combine A:B and B:C into A:B:C
Present/future ages in a ratio, or a number added to both terms changes the ratio
Successive increase/decrease, net % change, "by what % is B less than A" reversal
Marks/elections/population growth word problems with percentages
2-D figures: area/perimeter of triangle (Heron), square, rectangle, circle from given data
3-D solids: volume/surface area of cube, cylinder, cone, sphere and melting–recasting
Two/three workers with individual or pair rates – time together, or time for one alone
Men–days–hours (M₁D₁H₁ = M₂D₂H₂) and efficiency comparison
Train crossing a pole/platform/another train (relative speed, km/h ↔ m/s)
Average speed for equal distances, speed unit conversion, boats and streams
Simple interest: find SI, rate or time; sum becoming k times itself
Compound interest for 2–3 years (annual/half-yearly) and CI − SI difference
Profit/loss % from CP and SP, SP needed for a target gain, false weights
Marked price with one or two successive discounts; mark-up then discount profit %
Algebraic identities: given a + b and ab (or x + 1/x) find a² + b², a³ + b³ etc.
Triangle angle properties (angle sum, ratio of angles, angle between bisectors, exterior angle)
Standard trigonometric values and identities (sin²θ + cos²θ, tan θ from a given ratio)
Mean/median/mode of a small data set; mean after adding or removing an observation

archetypes.topic: Square Root, Age, Calendar & Clock, Pipes & Cistern
archetypes.pattern: Mixed short problems: pipes filling/emptying, age sums, odd days in calendar, angle between clock hands

Word-pair analogy: identify the relation in the first pair (instrument–quantity measured, worker–tool/workplace, organ–function, product–raw material) and pick the term that completes the second pair; distractors share the category but not the relation

Number or letter-cluster analogy: first pair linked by n² ± k, n³, n(n+1) or a fixed letter shift; apply the same rule to the third term; distractors come from the neighbouring rule (n² vs n²+1, etc.)
Number series – find the next/missing term; rules are increasing differences, ×n ± k, squares/cubes or primes; distractors are values from applying the rule with an off-by-one step
Letter or letter-cluster series: each letter in a cluster moves by a fixed/increasing step (+2, +3 …) or skips letters; choose the next cluster; distractors miss one letter shift
Letter-shift coding: a word is coded by shifting each letter (+k, alternating ±k, position-based shift or reverse + shift); find the code of a new word or decode a code
Number/position coding: word coded as sum or product of alphabet positions or reverse positions, or common-word sentence codes; find the code of a new word
Symbol substitution: + − × ÷ (or letters) are re-defined; substitute and evaluate with BODMAS; distractors come from left-to-right evaluation
Interchange two signs (or two numbers) so that the given equation becomes correct; check each option with BODMAS
Pointing/introduction statement (e.g. "only son of my father's …") – decode the chain to name the relation; gender trap built into distractors
Coded relations (A + B means A is mother of B …) or a family chain of 4–6 people – find how X is related to Y or which expression is true
Two or three categorical statements (All/Some/No) followed by two conclusions; pick Only I / Only II / Both / Neither; traps are reverse "All" conversions and possibility cases
Arrange 4–5 words in dictionary order (or a logical/meaningful sequence) and report the word at a given position or the correct order
Choose the Venn relationship (disjoint, one inside another, partial overlap) that best represents three given classes
Two-set counting: totals, "both" and "neither" figures given – find only-A / neither / both
Data sufficiency: a question with Statement I and II – decide whether I alone, II alone, either, both together or neither is sufficient
Short everyday statement (railway/civic/public notice) with two conclusions or courses of action – select which logically follow
Odd one out among four words from a common category (planets, units, instruments, organs) where one breaks the property
Odd number / number-pair / letter-cluster out: three follow a numeric rule (prime, n:n², fixed gap) and one does not
Linear row of 5–7 people facing north/south with immediate-left/right and "between" clues – find who sits at a position or between two people
Ranking/comparison: position from both ends of a row/class, or ordering by height/weight/marks from comparative statements
Circular table seating (facing centre) or day/floor scheduling with 5–6 entities – identify neighbour/position
Walk path with left/right turns and distances – find the shortest distance and direction from the start (Pythagoras triples)
Facing direction after a series of clockwise/anticlockwise turns, or shadow-based direction at sunrise/sunset
Statement (notice/advertisement/advice) with two assumptions – decide which are implicit
Should-type policy statement with Yes/No arguments – decide which arguments are strong
Mirror/water image of a letter–number string or clock time, or counting triangles/squares in a simple figure

archetypes.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
archetypes.pattern: Equations of motion numericals (v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as, free fall with g = 10 m/s²); distractors from forgetting ½ or using wrong sign

archetypes.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
archetypes.pattern: SI units, scalar vs vector, and Newton's laws concepts (inertia, action–reaction examples)

archetypes.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
archetypes.pattern: Momentum / F = ma / impulse numericals with unit conversion (g → kg, km/h → m/s)
Work, kinetic/potential energy and power numericals (W = Fs, KE = ½mv², PE = mgh, P = W/t) including "velocity doubled → KE ×4" type
Gravitation: universal law (effect of changing distance/mass), g on Moon, mass vs weight, free fall
Mirror/lens formula numericals: image distance, magnification, R = 2f; sign-convention traps in options
Refraction: refractive index and speed of light, power of lens P = 1/f (in metres), lens type from sign
Natural optical phenomena (scattering, total internal reflection, dispersion, twinkling) and defects of vision with correcting lens
Ohm's law and series/parallel resistance combinations – find equivalent resistance or current
Electric power and energy: P = VI = V²/R, kWh consumption and cost, heating effect (H = I²Rt)
Magnetic effects: Fleming's rules, right-hand thumb rule, motor vs generator, field lines, fuse/earthing
Wave numericals: v = fλ, time period, echo distance (2d = vt)
Properties of sound (audible range, infrasonic/ultrasonic, speed in media) and heat/temperature scale conversions
Atomic structure: protons/neutrons/electrons from Z and A, electronic configuration (K, L, M), valency, isotopes/isobars
Periodic table: group/period of an element from its configuration, trends in atomic size/metallic character, Döbereiner/Newlands/Mendeleev facts
Mole concept and molecular mass; states of matter, sublimation/evaporation concepts
Common salts – chemical formula/name/use of baking soda, washing soda, bleaching powder, Plaster of Paris, gypsum
pH scale and indicators (litmus, phenolphthalein, methyl orange), neutralisation and everyday acids
Metals: reactivity series & displacement, ores and extraction, alloys and their constituents, corrosion/rancidity
Carbon compounds: homologous series formula (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ etc.), functional groups, IUPAC names, allotropes of carbon
Identify the type of reaction (combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement, redox) from an equation
Oxidation–reduction: substance oxidised/reduced, oxidising agent; balancing coefficients
Diseases and their causative agents, vaccines, vitamin/mineral deficiency diseases
Human organ systems: digestive enzymes and organs, blood components, heart chambers, nervous system/brain parts, hormones
Plant life processes: photosynthesis requirements, xylem/phloem, transpiration, plant hormones and their functions
Mendel's monohybrid/dihybrid ratios, sex determination, evolution terms (homologous/analogous organs), food chains and ozone
Recent sports events (last 12–18 months): winner, runner-up or host city of a major tournament
Central government schemes/missions – launch year, objective or headline benefit (units, amount, beneficiaries)
National events, appointments to constitutional posts, awards and summits of the last year
Indian Railways and infrastructure news – new bridges, trains, safety systems and their location
Freedom-struggle movements, leaders, slogans, satyagrahas and their years
Ancient/medieval rulers, dynasties and the monuments or reforms associated with them
Which Article/Schedule of the Constitution deals with a right, duty or institution
Indian rivers, national parks, lakes and passes – the state or feature they belong to
Physical/world geography: soils, latitudes, atmosphere layers, oceans and continents
Economic institutions and terms – RBI functions, NITI Aayog, GST, budget/banking terms
Festivals, classical/folk dances and sports terms matched with states or games
Books and authors, important days, headquarters of organisations
ISRO missions and milestones, defence systems and the people associated with them

resources.notes: Question papers, provisional answer keys and response sheets are released by the RRBs only for the objection window after each CBT (e.g. 7–15 Sep 2026 for CEN 09/2025) via regional RRB websites such as https://www.rrbcdg.gov.in. There is no permanent official PYQ archive; memory-based shift papers are available from coaching publishers (unofficial).

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 11?
questions.explanation: Test for 11: difference of sums of alternate digits must be 0 or a multiple of 11. For 918291: (9 + 8 + 9) − (1 + 2 + 1) = 26 − 4 = 22, a multiple of 11. The others give 21, 20 and 4.

relevance.note: Which of four numbers divisible by 11 (verified 918291) - exact Group D divisibility format with near-identical options

questions.question: Simplify: 125 ÷ 5 of 5 + 3 × 4 − 2

relevance.note: 'of' precedence simplification with 37 left-to-right trap - Group D staple

questions.question: What is the value of 0.25 + 3/8 + 0.125?

relevance.note: Decimal+fraction sum - Group D fraction item, simple

questions.question: What is the HCF of 84 and 126?

relevance.note: Plain HCF of two numbers - in syllabus but more elementary than typical Group D HCF/LCM word items

questions.question: The present ages of two brothers are in the ratio 5 : 7. After 6 years the ratio will be 3 : 4. What is the present age of the elder brother?

relevance.note: Age ratio 5:7 to 3:4 after 6 years - Group D ages item with younger-brother trap 30

questions.question: A student scored 342 marks out of 450. What percentage of marks did he score?

relevance.note: Marks percentage single division - easier than Group D percentage word problems

questions.question: What is the area of a triangle whose sides are 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm?

relevance.note: Heron 13-14-15 = 84 - Group D asks this exact triangle; well-known

questions.question: 12 men can complete a piece of work in 15 days. How many men are needed to complete the same work in 9 days?
questions.explanation: Total work = 12 × 15 = 180 man-days. Men needed = 180 ÷ 9 = 20.

relevance.note: M1D1=M2D2 men-days - Group D staple

questions.question: What is the compound interest on ₹8,000 at 5% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?

relevance.note: CI 2 years with SI 800 trap - Group D CI item

questions.question: By selling an article for ₹1,140, a man loses 5%. At what price should he sell it to gain 5%?

relevance.note: SP for 5% gain from 5% loss - Group D profit-loss exact style

questions.question: If a + b = 10 and ab = 21, what is the value of a² + b²?

relevance.note: a²+b² from a+b and ab - Group D algebra

questions.question: What is the value of sin²30° + cos²60° + tan²45°?

relevance.note: Standard trig values sum - Group D trig item

questions.question: What is the median of the data 7, 3, 9, 12, 5, 10?
questions.explanation: Arranged: 3, 5, 7, 9, 10, 12. With 6 values the median is the average of the 3rd and 4th: (7 + 9)/2 = 8.

relevance.note: Median of even-count unsorted data - Group D statistics with unsorted trap

questions.question: Eye : See :: Ear : ?
questions.explanation: The eye is the organ used to see; the ear is the organ used to hear.

relevance.note: Organ:function analogy; Eye:See is too obvious, distractors weak (Sound)

questions.question: Select the number that completes the analogy. 25 : 125 :: 36 : ?
questions.explanation: 25 = 5², 125 = 5³. Similarly 36 = 6², so the answer is 6³ = 216.

relevance.note: n²:n³ analogy (25:125 → 36:216) - Group D number analogy

questions.question: Find the next number: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, ?
questions.explanation: Terms are n² + 1 for n = 1 to 5. Next = 6² + 1 = 37 (differences 3, 5, 7, 9, 11).

relevance.note: n²+1 series - Group D series easy

questions.question: Find the next letter: B, E, I, N, ?
questions.explanation: Positions 2, 5, 9, 14 increase by +3, +4, +5; next is 14 + 6 = 20 = T.

relevance.note: Letter series +3,+4,+5,+6 - Group D letter series

questions.question: Find the next number: 4, 9, 25, 49, 121, ?
questions.explanation: These are squares of consecutive primes 2, 3, 5, 7, 11. Next prime is 13, and 13² = 169.

relevance.note: Squares of primes series with 144 (12²) trap - Group D style

questions.question: In a certain code, SMART is written as TRAMS. How will TRAIN be written in that code?
questions.explanation: The word is written in reverse order: TRAIN → NIART.

relevance.note: Reverse-word coding - Group D coding variant

questions.question: If A means '+', B means '−', C means '×' and D means '÷', what is the value of 18 D 3 C 4 A 5 B 6?

relevance.note: Letter-to-operator substitution with BODMAS - Group D exact

questions.question: A is the brother of B. C is the father of A. D is the mother of C. How is D related to B?
questions.explanation: C is the father of A and hence of B (A and B are siblings). D is C's mother, so D is B's grandmother.

relevance.note: Four-person family chain - Group D blood relation

questions.question:
Statements: All cats are dogs. All dogs are birds.
Conclusions: I. All cats are birds. II. Some birds are cats.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: Cats ⊂ Dogs ⊂ Birds, so all cats are birds (I). Converting I gives 'Some birds are cats' (II).

relevance.note: All-All syllogism with conversion conclusion - Group D exact

questions.question: Arrange the following in a logical sequence: 1. Seed 2. Plant 3. Fruit 4. Flower 5. Sapling
questions.explanation: A seed grows into a sapling, then a plant, which bears flowers that develop into fruits.

relevance.note: Logical sequence seed-sapling-plant-flower-fruit - Group D meaningful-order item

questions.question: In a class of 50 students, 28 play cricket, 20 play football and 8 play both. How many students play only cricket?
questions.explanation: Only cricket = 28 − 8 = 20.

relevance.note: Only-cricket from two-set data with 28 total trap - Group D counting

questions.question: Select the odd one out: Mercury, Venus, Moon, Mars
questions.explanation: Mercury, Venus and Mars are planets; the Moon is a natural satellite of Earth.

relevance.note: Moon (satellite) among planets - Group D odd-one-out

questions.question: A, B, C, D and E stand in a row facing north. A is second from the left end. C is to the immediate right of A. B is at the right end. D stands between C and B. Who is at the left end?
questions.explanation: A = 2, C = 3, B = 5, so D = 4 (between C and B). The only remaining place, 1, goes to E.

relevance.note: 5-person row straightforward - Group D linear arrangement

questions.question: Ravi is facing east. He turns 90° clockwise and then turns 180°. In which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: East → 90° clockwise → South → 180° → North.

relevance.note: Turns from east clockwise then 180 - Group D direction

questions.question:
Statement: 'Use our new water purifier to keep your family healthy.' – an advertisement.
Assumptions: I. Clean drinking water helps keep people healthy. II. People want to keep their families healthy.
Which assumption(s) are implicit?
options: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.explanation: The advert links purified water to health (I) and appeals to the desire to keep the family healthy (II); both are assumed.

relevance.note: Advertisement both assumptions implicit - Group D assumption item

questions.question:
Question: What is Ravi's present age?
Statement I: Ravi is 5 years older than Sunil.
Statement II: Sunil's age is half of Ravi's age.
Which statement(s) are sufficient to answer the question?
options: Both I and II together are needed
Either I or II alone is sufficient
questions.explanation: Neither statement alone gives a value. Together: R = S + 5 and S = R/2 ⇒ R = R/2 + 5 ⇒ R = 10 years.

relevance.note: Data sufficiency ages needing both - Group D DS format

questions.question: Among P, Q, R, S and T, each has a different height. R is taller than P and S. P is taller than Q. S is taller than P. T is taller than R. Who is the third tallest?
questions.explanation: T > R; R > S; S > P; P > Q. The full order is T > R > S > P > Q, so S is third tallest.

relevance.note: Height comparison third tallest - Group D ranking

questions.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
questions.question: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s² for 5 s. What distance does it cover in this time?
questions.explanation: s = ut + ½at² = 0 + ½ × 2 × 5² = 25 m.

relevance.note: s=ut+½at² with 50 m (forgot ½) trap - Group D motion numerical exact

questions.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
questions.question: Newton's first law of motion is also known as the:
questions.explanation: The first law states that a body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted on by an external force – the property called inertia.

relevance.note: First law = law of inertia - Group D Newton concept

questions.question: What is the kinetic energy of a body of mass 2 kg moving with a velocity of 3 m/s?
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 3² = 9 J.

relevance.note: KE ½mv² = 9 J with 18 J (no ½) trap - Group D exact

questions.question: The refractive index of glass is 1.5. If the speed of light in vacuum is 3 × 10⁸ m/s, what is the speed of light in glass?

relevance.note: v = c/n in glass - Group D refraction numerical, 4.5 (multiply) trap

questions.question: Three resistors of 6 Ω each are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?

relevance.note: Parallel equal resistors R/n - Group D resistance item with series 18 trap

questions.question: An electric bulb is rated 100 W, 220 V. What is the resistance of its filament when glowing?

relevance.note: R = V²/P = 484 Ω - Group D electric power numerical

questions.question: An element has atomic number 17. What is its valency?
questions.explanation: Electronic configuration is 2, 8, 7. It needs 1 electron to complete its octet, so its valency is 1 (it is chlorine).

relevance.note: Valency from Z=17 with 7 (valence electrons) trap - Group D atomic structure exact

questions.question: Blue litmus paper turns red when it is dipped in:
questions.explanation: Acids turn blue litmus red. NaOH solution and lime water are bases; distilled water is neutral.

relevance.note: Litmus colour change with acid - Group D indicator item

questions.question: What is the chemical formula of Plaster of Paris?
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, CaSO₄·½H₂O. CaSO₄·2H₂O is gypsum.

relevance.note: PoP formula vs gypsum trap - Group D common salts exact

questions.question: What is the general formula of alkynes?
questions.explanation: Alkanes are CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, alkenes CₙH₂ₙ and alkynes (one triple bond) CₙH₂ₙ₋₂, e.g. ethyne C₂H₂.

relevance.note: Alkyne general formula with alkane/alkene traps - Group D carbon compounds

questions.question: The reaction 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO is an example of which type of reaction?
questions.explanation: Two reactants combine to form a single product, so it is a combination reaction (it is also an oxidation of magnesium).

relevance.note: Identify combination reaction from equation - Group D reaction-type

questions.question: In plants, the xylem tissue mainly transports:
questions.explanation: Xylem carries water and dissolved minerals from roots to leaves; phloem transports prepared food.

relevance.note: Xylem function vs phloem trap - Group D plant transport

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
questions.explanation: Measles is a viral disease. Typhoid, cholera and tuberculosis are caused by bacteria.

relevance.note: Viral disease among bacterial ones - Group D disease-agent item

questions.question: In August 2023, India's Chandrayaan-3 mission made a soft landing in which region of the Moon?
questions.explanation: On 23 August 2023 the Vikram lander touched down near the south pole of the Moon, making India the first country to land in that region.

relevance.note: Chandrayaan-3 south pole - asked often in Group D 2025; well-worn but valid

questions.question: Who gave the slogan 'Do or Die' during the Quit India Movement?
questions.explanation: Gandhiji gave the call 'Do or Die' at the Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, in August 1942.

relevance.note: 'Do or Die' slogan-leader - Group D freedom-struggle slogan item

questions.question: In which year did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place?
questions.explanation: The massacre took place at Amritsar on 13 April 1919.

relevance.note: Jallianwala Bagh 1919 - Group D year-of-event item

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability?
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability. Article 14 is equality before law, 21 is right to life and 32 is constitutional remedies.

relevance.note: Art 17 untouchability - Group D Article question

questions.question: The Sundarbans delta is formed mainly by which rivers?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans lie in the Ganga–Brahmaputra (–Meghna) delta in West Bengal and Bangladesh.

relevance.note: Sundarbans delta rivers - Group D river geography; labelled hard but easy

questions.question: Kaziranga National Park, famous for the one-horned rhinoceros, is in which state?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is in Assam.

relevance.note: Kaziranga-Assam - Group D park-state staple

questions.question: NITI Aayog replaced which body in January 2015?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog was set up on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission (1950).

relevance.note: NITI Aayog replaced Planning Commission - Group D economy institution

questions.question: Pongal is a harvest festival mainly celebrated in which state?
questions.explanation: Pongal is the harvest festival of Tamil Nadu, celebrated in mid-January.

relevance.note: Pongal-Tamil Nadu - Group D festival-state

questions.question: 'Wings of Fire' is the autobiography of:
questions.explanation: 'Wings of Fire' (1999) is the autobiography of Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, written with Arun Tiwari.

relevance.note: Wings of Fire-Kalam with scientist distractors - Group D books-authors

questions.question: Who is regarded as the father of the Indian space programme?
questions.explanation: Dr Vikram Sarabhai founded INCOSPAR (1962) which became ISRO; he is called the father of India's space programme.

relevance.note: Father of Indian space programme Sarabhai vs Bhabha trap - Group D ISRO people

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 8?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 8 if its last three digits are. 512 ÷ 8 = 64 exactly, whereas 324, 612 and 436 leave remainders 4, 4 and 4.

relevance.note: Divisible by 8 via last three digits - Group D exact

questions.question: What is the unit digit of 3⁶⁵ × 7⁴²?
questions.explanation: Powers of 3 and 7 repeat their unit digits every 4. 65 = 4 × 16 + 1, so 3⁶⁵ ends in 3; 42 = 4 × 10 + 2, so 7⁴² ends in 9. 3 × 9 = 27 → unit digit 7.

relevance.note: Unit digit of product of powers of 3 and 7 - Group D cyclicity

questions.question: Simplify: 84 ÷ 4 of 3 + 6 × 5 − 12
questions.explanation: "of" is done first: 4 of 3 = 12. Then 84 ÷ 12 = 7, 6 × 5 = 30. 7 + 30 − 12 = 25. (Ignoring "of" and working left to right gives 81.)

relevance.note: 'of' precedence simplification with 37 trap - Group D staple

questions.question: What is the value of √1764 + 10 × √0.81?

relevance.note: Square roots of perfect square and decimal - Group D roots item

questions.question: Which of the following fractions is the largest: 5/8, 7/11, 3/5, 9/14?

relevance.note: Largest of four close fractions - Group D compare fractions

questions.question: What is the least number which, when divided by 12, 15 and 20, leaves a remainder of 7 in each case?
questions.explanation: LCM of 12, 15 and 20 = 60. Required number = 60 + 7 = 67. (127 also leaves remainder 7 but is not the least.)

relevance.note: LCM + remainder - Group D least-number exact

questions.question: ₹5,400 is divided among P, Q and R in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. How much more does R get than P?

relevance.note: Ratio division difference R−P - Group D ratio

questions.question: The population of a town is 25,000. It increases by 8% in the first year and by 10% in the second year. What is the population after two years?
questions.explanation: After year 1: 25,000 × 1.08 = 27,000. After year 2: 27,000 × 1.10 = 29,700. (Adding 18% directly gives 29,500.)

relevance.note: Population successive increase - Group D population item

questions.question: The area of a circle is 616 cm². What is its circumference? (Take π = 22/7)
